Formula guide

NeuroBlast Ingredients & Formula

A practical overview of the five ingredients identified in current cognitive-support materials, with an emphasis on label verification and responsible interpretation.

The five-ingredient formula

Current NeuroBlast cognitive-support materials identify GABA, L-Glutamine, L-Tryptophan, Eleutherococcus senticosus, and L-Carnitine Base.

Some available product descriptions do not state a milligram amount for each ingredient. That makes the current Supplement Facts panel particularly important when comparing the product with research on individual ingredients.

GABA

A neurotransmitter involved in inhibitory signaling in the nervous system. Product materials associate it with a calmer, clearer mental state.

L-Glutamine

An amino acid with roles in metabolism and nervous-system biology. The product materials position it around everyday neuronal support.

L-Tryptophan

An amino acid used by the body to make serotonin and other compounds. Its presence does not establish a particular finished-product outcome.

Eleutherococcus senticosus

A botanical commonly known as eleuthero or Siberian ginseng. Product materials position it around resilience and everyday wellness.

L-Carnitine Base

A compound involved in cellular energy metabolism. NeuroBlast materials include it as part of the five-ingredient formula.

What is not established

The presence of these ingredients alone does not prove that the finished product delivers a specific cognitive outcome.

Why dose information matters

Research findings depend on dose, formulation, population, duration, and study design. If a product page does not provide a clear amount for an ingredient, it is difficult to compare the finished product directly with a particular research protocol.

  • Check the serving size on the current label.
  • Confirm the amount of each active ingredient where provided.
  • Review other ingredients and potential allergens.
  • Do not assume that “more” is automatically better.
  • Discuss supplement use with a qualified professional when medications or health conditions are relevant.

Formula verification note

Ingredient lists and formulations can change. The current product label should take priority over older articles, screenshots, or secondary websites. If the current information differs from older descriptions, use the current label for purchase and use decisions.
